WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Long-Horizon Visual Web Agents
                          with Realistic Tasks

                                                                 Visual web agents for realistic tasks. We focus on vi-
    Recent work has demonstrated that vision-language mod-       sual web agents that take screenshots as input and output
els can be adapted into web agents via supervised fine-tuning    browser actions. General-purpose VLMs (Gemma3 [11],
and task-specific training pipelines [16]. However, in con-      GLM-4.1v [16], Qwen3-VL [5]) and web-specific agents
trast to the rapid progress of online reinforcement learn-       (UI-TARS [30]) have shown strong results on such tasks.
ing (RL) in text-only domains such as software engineering          Evaluation benchmarks and training environments.
and mathematical reasoning [24, 33], scaling RL for visual       Robust evaluation benchmarks have advanced substantially
web agents remains substantially more challenging. Unlike        (WebVoyager [14], Mind2Web-Live [25], Mind2Web-2 [12],
text-based settings, where rollouts are fast and rewards are     InSTA [36], BrowseComp [37], GAIA [23]), while training
easily verifiable, visual web tasks require reasoning over       environments remain scarce. WebRL [29] and PAE [46]
fine-grained rendered interfaces and often lack unambiguous      have limited task diversity and unoptimized rollout systems.
success signals [17, 32, 42]. Addressing these challenges        WebGym addresses both via rubric-derived decomposition
requires three ingredients: a large, diverse task set spanning   and asynchronous rollouts.
many domains and difficulty levels to encourage generaliz-           Scaling online RL for training agents. Scaling on-
able policy learning, clear evaluation protocols that provide     line RL trajectories boosts agent capabilities with REIN-
meaningful learning signals, and high rollout speed, since        FORCE [38] across software engineering [24], math [33],
simulating web browsers dominates wall-clock time [46].           and deep research [15, 19, 44]. WebGym builds on these
                                                                  insights with a large, diverse task set and on-policy RL.
   To advance scaling of training recipes for visual web
agents, we introduce WebGym, a training environment fea-
turing the largest open-source task set and the fastest           3. Tasks in WebGym and Evaluation Protocol
rollout system to date (to our knowledge) for training web
agents. Specifically, WebGym provides (1) a task set with        Training with online RL requires a large number of model-
nearly 300,000 tasks spanning a wide range of difficulties,      generated rollouts guided by reliable reward signals on a
domains, and evaluation criteria, enabling agents to gen-        family of tasks (“environments” in traditional multi-task
eralize across diverse and challenging scenarios, and (2)        RL nomenclature) that we curate. To learn generalizable
an efficient asynchronous rollout system capable of collect-     policies with such a procedure, the task set must (1) span
ing 1,800 trajectories with an average of 13.2 steps in just     diverse domains and websites, (2) cover a range of “diffi-
30 minutes using 128 CPUs and 24 NVIDIA H100 GPUs.               culties” from atomic to compositional tasks, and (3) include
This achieves a 4-5× speedup compared to traditional syn-        verifiable evaluators that translate outcomes into meaningful
chronous rollout systems. We study three dimensions of           learning signals. Existing web agent benchmarks, while ef-
scaling the task set in WebGym: task set breadth, depth          fective for evaluation, are typically too small and static for
and size, and observe significant improvements over each         large-scale training. Existing training tasks are either non-
dimension with the task set introduced in WebGym. We             diverse [46] and lack a wide range of task difficulties [36],
demonstrate that a simple REINFORCE-like algorithm can           or do not come paired with good task-level evaluation crite-
improve Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B to state-of-the-art perfor-         ria, rubrics, or guidance for enabling robust policy evalua-
mance on web agent benchmarks across tasks from easy to          tion [23, 36, 37, 40, 46]. We describe how we procedurally
long-horizon in out-of-domain settings.                          construct a task set that satisfies these desiderata.
